subject: Budget range validation - Novalytics (token volumes & procurement thresholds)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@novalytics.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@novalytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Budget range validation - Novalytics (token volumes & procurement thresholds)

Hi Jordan / procurement team —

Thanks again for the time today — loved the walkthrough of your support automation use case. Quick recap and two asks so we can move pricing/contracting forward: 

Recap:
- Primary use: customer support triage + automated suggested responses (mix of short-gen + instruction-following).
- Expected queries: ~1.2M NLUs per month (avg 40 tokens per request currently).
- Peak SLA: <300ms 95p for chat-turns; can accept async batch for bulk backfill.

Asks:
1) Can you confirm expected monthly token volume bands? You mentioned a pilot at ~500k requests/month — if you can provide the monthly token estimate (tokens/month) that helps us pick the right Dedicated vs Hosted plan. I attached a quick usage template to make this easy.
2) Procurement thresholds: do you have internal thresholds for vendor spend that would change contracting steps (e.g., >$50k needs legal review, >$200k requires finance approval, etc.)? That will affect whether we propose a simple PO or a full SOW + enterprise terms.

Prelim pricing context: based on a few similar customers, the unit economics typically land between $700–$1,300 per 1M tokens depending on batching/quantization and SLA. We can tune this after we see your token profile.

Next steps: if you can reply with a) token/month band (best-effort) and b) procurement approval thresholds, I’ll put together 2 budget bands (pilot and 12-month run-rate) and a recommended target $/1M tokens.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments:
- Novalytics_Monthly_Usage_Template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@novalytics.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@novalytics.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@novalytics.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Novalytics (token volumes & procurement thresholds)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the follow-up and the template — attaching filled version inline (see attached). High-level numbers:
- Pilot (months 1–3): ~500k requests/month x 40 tokens/request => ~20M tokens/month.
- Post-pilot expected growth (months 4–12): 1.0–1.5M requests/month => ~40–60M tokens/month.
- Long-term steady-state (12+ months): targeting 1.2–1.4M requests/month => ~48–56M tokens/month.

Procurement thresholds:
- Purchase orders under $25k: standard PO, no legal review.
- $25k–$100k: procurement + finance approval; legal sees commercial terms but limited review.
- >$100k: full legal + security review and SOW required.

For context, our CFO prefers to keep first-year vendor commitments under $100k if possible, but we can stretch for clear ROI.

Also Samira (cc) will handle SOC 2/security questionnaire — she may request evidence.

Jordan
Jordan Miller
Head of Product, Novalytics
jordan.miller@novalytics.ai

Attachment: Novalytics_Monthly_Usage_Template.xlsx (filled)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Budget range validation - Novalytics (token volumes & procurement thresholds)

Looping you in — Jordan confirmed the bands which line up with a mid-market expansion opportunity. A few thoughts: 

- Volume bands: pilot 20M tokens/mo, growth 40–60M tokens/mo. That suggests our postcard pricing should include a pilot band (up to 25M tokens) and a production band (40–60M tokens).
- Procurement threshold: >$100k triggers full legal + security review. CFO preference to keep first-year < $100k is important.

Pricing recommendation (internal):
- Pilot (20M tokens/mo): propose hosted discounted rate targeting ~$1,200 per 1M tokens, with a 3-month commitment credit to get them started. That keeps first-year commitment below $100k if they stay at pilot scale for first quarter.
- Production run-rate (48–56M tokens/mo): target $800–$1,000 per 1M tokens for a 12-month committed plan (the lower bound assumes some batching/quantization gains).

If legal/security will be triggered at >$100k, we should propose a phased SOW: 3-month pilot (hosted), followed by 12-month committed capacity if metrics meet SLA and cost targets. That minimizes procurement friction.

Action items: Alex — can you confirm which target $/1M tokens you want to present to Jordan? I can draft a 2-option pricing table and lightweight SOW. Also Samira will need SOC2 evidence; I attached the SOC2_evidence_summary we usually send.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: SOC2_evidence_summary.pdf

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@novalytics.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@novalytics.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@novalytics.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget range validation - Novalytics (token volumes & procurement thresholds)

Jordan / Samira / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick numbers — super helpful. To be pragmatic and avoid triggering full legal review on day 1, here's what we'd like to propose: 

Option A — Pilot-first (lowest friction)
- 3-month hosted pilot: up to 25M tokens/month flat-rate credit + metered overage at $1,200 per 1M tokens.
- Estimated first-year spend if they convert at growth: ~$85k–$110k (depending on timing of conversion).

Option B — Phased committed (faster unit economics)
- 12-month committed plan for 48M tokens/month, target price $900 per 1M tokens with standard SLA and SOC2 evidence. 12-month commitment will require SOW and legal review (likely >$100k).

Given your CFO note about keeping year one under $100k, Option A with the 3-month ramp is the least procurement friction and gets them live quickly. If you want, Marissa will put together the 2-option pricing table + a short SOW for Option B.

Next step: Would you be available for a 30-min call next week (Thu 3/12 or Fri 3/13) to review the options and timeline? I can bring a sample SOW and the SOC2 summary link.

Link to sample SOW & signature: https://app.docusign.com/recipient/abcdefg12345

Thanks — looking forward.

— Alex
Alex Martinez
